names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 20 Οκτωβρίου, «Άγιοι Ζεβινάς, Γερμανός, Νικηφόρος και Αντωνίνος», with the rank word left off.

The heading of the calendar's name link behind his place in the line for 13 ноября ст. ст., page 225, «Антонин (Антоний) Кесарийский (Палестинский), пресвитер, сщмч.», with the grade and the rank words left off. Both bracketed words are the calendar's own: the first is a second form of the forename, the second the province behind the city. The line itself declines the name and gives no by-name at all, «Мчч. Антонина , Никифора и Германа».

death.note: Two calendars, two readings, and the interval holds both. saint.gr: «Οι Άγιοι αυτοί μαρτύρησαν επί Μαξιμιανού (286-305)» — the reign and no year. days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 13 ноября ст. ст. closes «(ок. 308)», which is outside that reign; neither is preferred here.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 ноября ст. ст. — «Мчч. Антонина , Никифора и Германа (ок. 308).»

attestations.note: Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 20ης Οκτωβρίου — «Άγιοι Ζεβινάς, Γερμανός, Νικηφόρος και Αντωνίνος»

attestations.note: The life page `https://www.saint.gr/810/saint.aspx` heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 20 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and tells one story for the four of them: they suffered under Maximian, whose reign the page dates 286–305; Antoninus was an old man and the other three were young; they were arrested at Caesarea by one Mazos because they were Christians, and beheaded. The page adds «Η μνήμη τους επαναλαμβάνεται και την 12η Νοεμβρίου, μαζί με την Αγία Μαναθώ, που εσφαλμένα εκεί αναφέρεται ως Μαραθώ» — a second Greek day, recorded here as a note because one attestation row per church is the schema. No hymn is printed for them, and neither the listing nor the life page carries the asterisk or the «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The corpus holds no martyr of this name in this company; the nearest same-name folders belong to other days and other companies.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (1 October 2026).
